title: Electrostatic shielding and equilibrium
stem: An isolated a solid conducting ball is placed in a static external electric field and allowed to reach electrostatic equilibrium.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe the rearrangement of free charge and the resultant field within the conducting material.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why field lines meet the conducting surface at right angles in electrostatic equilibrium.

steps.text: Free charges move under the applied field and build up on the surface.
Their induced field cancels the applied field within the conducting material, making the resultant field zero.
Any tangential field would exert a force on free surface charges and cause continuing motion.
Equilibrium therefore requires zero tangential component.

title: Electrostatic shielding and equilibrium
stem: An isolated a closed hollow conducting shell with no charge in its cavity is placed in a static external electric field and allowed to reach electrostatic equilibrium.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe the rearrangement of free charge and the resultant field within the conducting material.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why field lines meet the conducting surface at right angles in electrostatic equilibrium.

steps.text: Free charges move under the applied field and build up on the surface.
Their induced field cancels the applied field within the conducting material, making the resultant field zero.
Any tangential field would exert a force on free surface charges and cause continuing motion.
Equilibrium therefore requires zero tangential component.

title: A coil opposes a changing current
stem: The current magnitude in a coil is increasing while its direction remains fixed. Discuss the induced emf in the coil itself. No numerical inductance formula is required.

steps.text: The current produces a magnetic field and magnetic flux linked with the coil.

title: Entering and leaving a finite field region
stem: A rectangular coil has 40 turns, height $0.15\,\mathrm{m}$ and width $0.1\,\mathrm{m}$ along its horizontal direction of motion. It moves right at $0.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ through a uniform field $0.28\,\mathrm{T}$ into the page. The field region has width $0.3\,\mathrm{m}$ along the motion and extends far enough vertically. At $t=0$ the leading edge just enters. Define flux into the page as positive.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum flux linkage.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the induced-emf magnitudes and the entry and exit time intervals.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Give the signs of the entry and exit emf and explain why they differ.

steps.text: While an edge crosses the boundary, $|\mathcal E|=NBhv$ and each crossing lasts $w/v$.
Magnitude $0.84\,\mathrm{V}$ during $0<t<0.2\,\mathrm{s}$ and $0.6<t<0.8\,\mathrm{s}$; zero between these intervals.
Entry emf is negative and exit emf positive for the stated flux orientation.
The linked positive flux increases on entry and decreases on exit; Faraday's law puts a minus sign in front of its time derivative.

subject: physics-hl
title: A coil opposes a changing current
stem: The current magnitude in a coil is decreasing while its direction remains fixed. Discuss the induced emf in the coil itself. No numerical inductance formula is required.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Explain how a changing current leads to an induced emf.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State the effect of this emf on the current change.

steps.text: The current produces a magnetic field and magnetic flux linked with the coil.
A changing current changes that linked flux, producing an induced emf.
It opposes the decreasing current change, according to Lenz's law.
For a rising current it acts against the supply; for a falling current it tends to keep the original current flowing.
